papers.title: A Geometric Coding Theorem
papers.abstract: This paper establishes a direct analogue of the classical Coding Theorem in the setting of symmetry groups. We consider computable bijections on the set of binary strings and define the symmetry prior of a string x as the probability that a randomly chosen symmetry from a given group G has x as its unique fixed point. We show that for any fix-retractable symmetry group G, a group admitting a computable section that selects an isolating symmetry for every string, the symmetry prior is a universal lower semi-computable semi-measure. In this case, the Geometric Coding Theorem holds. This result is a coding-theoretic restatement of a theorem of Trejo, Kreinovich and Longpr\'e, who showed that the complexity of describing a string by a symmetry with that string as its unique fixed point equals its Kolmogorov complexity. Our contribution is to recast it in terms of algorithmic probability and to treat the symmetry group as a parameter, identifying fix-retractability as exactly the condition under which symmetry complexity collapses onto Kolmogorov complexity.

papers.title: Categorified Koszul duality and deformation theory of higher categories
papers.abstract: This paper develops a deformation theory for stable $(\infty,n)$-categories for $n > 1$. We introduce the framework of complete $t$-structured stable presentable $(\infty,n)$-categories. Within this setting, we establish a higher categorified Koszul duality among complete $t$-structured presentable $(\infty,n)$-categories. Using this duality, we develop the deformation theory. We prove that the deformation problem for such categories is a well-behaved formal moduli problem determined by Hochschild cohomology, and we deduce the corresponding obstruction theory. Finally, we apply our results to sheaves of categories on perfect stacks.

papers.title: Finite regularity moduli stacks through diffeology
papers.abstract: Diffeological non-Abelian Hodge theory motivates the study of $C^r$ families of Higgs bundles and flat bundles for finite $r$. In this article, we provide a uniform language for treating moduli stacks parametrizing such objects in terms of diffeology. More specifically, we develop a theory of stacks presentable by diffeological groupoids over the site of $C^r$ manifolds for arbitrary $r$. As an application, we construct moduli stacks over the sites of $C^r$ manifolds parametrizing $C^r$ vector bundles over a smooth manifold, and $C^r$ families of Higgs bundles and of flat bundles over a complex manifold. We also construct $C^r$ versions of the non-Abelian Hodge filtration stack, interpolating between Higgs bundles and flat bundles through $\lambda$--connections. We show that all these stacks are presentable by diffeological groupoids. Finally, we construct moduli stacks parametrizing $C^r$ families of $\Delta^n$--shaped diagrams of these objects, and show that they assemble into simplicial stacks whose levels are all presentable by diffeological groupoids.

papers.title: An $\infty$-category approach to $A_\infty$-algebras and $A_\infty$-categories
papers.abstract: $A_\infty$-algebras over a commutative ring $R$ are generalizations of $R$-algebras in which multiplication is only associative up to higher homotopies. Similarly, $A_\infty$-categories over $R$ are generalizations of $R$-linear categories in which composition of morphisms is only associative up to higher homotopies. They are important in the definition of Fukaya categories in Symplectic Geometry, and in other areas of mathematics. By $\infty$-categories we mean quasicategories, a class of simplicial sets which are a model for $(\infty,1)$-categories, used in the work of Jacob Lurie. We define and study $\infty$-categories of $A_\infty$-algebras and $A_\infty$-categories. Our approach is unusual in that rather than defining them by localization, we construct our $\infty$-categories completely explicitly as simplicial sets. Our $\infty$-categories are intended for applications to Fukaya categories in Symplectic Geometry. Given a suitable symplectic manifold $(X,\omega)$, one should construct its Fukaya category ${\mathscr F}(X,\omega)$, a (filtered) $A_\infty$-category, and its derived Fukaya category $D^b{\mathscr F}(X,\omega)$, a triangulated category (or better, a stable $\infty$-category). Typically ${\mathscr F}(X,\omega)$ depends on many arbitrary choices. Our $\infty$-categories give a clean way to explain in what sense ${\mathscr F}(X,\omega)$ and $D^b{\mathscr F}(X,\omega)$ are independent of these choices.

papers.title: Semi-exact functors and the conjecture of Coulembier and Flake
papers.abstract: We introduce the notion of semi-exact functors between abelian categories, which are characterised by either preserving or breaking exactness of sequences. We prove semi-exact functors are always exact with respect to a canonically determined exact structure. For a symmetric tensor category $\Cs$, we define a support theory by considering all $\Bbbk$-linear symmetric monoidal, semi-exact functors $\mathscr{C}\to\operatorname{Ver}_{p^\infty}$ up to equivalence, and conjecture that it agrees with the Balmer spectrum of the stable category when $\mathscr{C}$ is finite. We prove a weak form of this conjecture and other results for Tannakian categories and in characteristic 0. Critical to the positive characteristic case is a functor constructed by Coulembier and Flake who were interested in higher Frobenius functors. We show that their construction, which relies on the theory of abelian envelopes, gives a natural source for semi-exact functors, and at least in the Tannakian setting gives all $\Bbbk$-linear, symmetric monoidal, semi-exact functors.

papers.title: Auslander correspondence for proper connective DG-algebras via extended module categories
papers.abstract: We establish a $d$-dimensional Auslander correspondence for $d$-truncated proper connective DG-algebras via $d$-extended module categories. A $d$-truncated proper connective DG-algebra $\Gamma$ is called Auslander if its $d$-extended module category is a $d$-Auslander extriangulated category. Our main theorem gives a one-to-one correspondence: for any $d$-truncated proper connective DG-algebra $\Lambda$ whose $d$-extended module category has finitely many indecomposable objects, the endomorphism DG-algebra of an additive generator is Auslander, and conversely every Auslander $d$-truncated proper connective DG-algebra arises in this way.

papers.title: From Multirelations to Meet-Relations: A Relational Duality for Semilattices with Adjunctions
papers.abstract: We develop a relational duality for semilattices with adjunctions (SLatas) based on binary meet-relations. First, we introduce the category of MoS-spaces and establish a dual equivalence with modal semilattices. Then, by means of A-relations, we define the category RelSP and prove a dual equivalence between SLata and RelSP. To compare this framework with the multirelational semantics previously developed for SLatas, we introduce the notion of normal mS-space and show that, under this condition, the multirelational structure can be canonically recovered from a meet-relation, and conversely. As a consequence, we prove that the categories RelSP and SLataSp are isomorphic.

papers.title: Euclidean interval objects in categories with finite products
papers.abstract: Based on the intuitive notion of convexity, we formulate a universal property defining interval objects in a category with finite products. Interval objects are structures corresponding to closed intervals of the real line, but their definition does not assume a pre-existing notion of real number. The universal property characterises such structures up to isomorphism, supports the definition of functions between intervals, and provides a means of verifying identities between functions. In the category of sets, the universal property characterises closed intervals of real numbers with nonempty interior. In the category of topological spaces, we obtain intervals with the Euclidean topology. We also prove that every elementary topos with natural numbers object contains an interval object; furthermore, we characterise interval objects as intervals of real numbers in the Cauchy completion of the rational numbers within the Dedekind reals.

papers.title: Morphisms and comorphisms of sites I -- Double categories of sites
papers.abstract: We arrange morphisms and comorphisms of sites as the horizontal and vertical cells of a double category of sites; using the formalism of extensions and restrictions of presheaves, we explains how one can define a sheafification double functor from this double category to the quintet double category of Grothendieck topoi. We describe properties of this double functor and recover some classical results of topos theory through a new notion of locally exact square, generalizing exact squares in the presence of topologies. We also describe a 2-comonad on $\Cat$ for which lax morphisms of coalgebras are morphisms of sites and colax morphisms are comorphisms of sites, explaining the arrangement as a double category.
